record.original_question: Can one prove special cases of one of the two conjectures discussed in Section 13 from known cases of the other conjecture?

evidence.quote: Problem 13.2. Prove one of the above two conjectures for some special case from the known case of the other conjecture.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $k$ be a number field with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_k$.

(A) Malle's conjecture. For a finite transitive subgroup $G\subset S_n$, let
$$N_k(G;X)=\#\{K/k\ \text{(in a fixed algebraic closure)}: [K:k]=n,\ \operatorname{Gal}(K^{\mathrm{gal}}/k)\simeq G\ \text{as permutation group},\ |\operatorname{Disc}(K/k)|\le X\}.$$
Malle's conjecture predicts the existence of explicit constants $a(G)\in\mathbb{Q}_{>0}$ and $b(k,G)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ and a positive constant $c(k,G)$ such that
$$N_k(G;X)\sim c(k,G)\,X^{a(G)}(\log X)^{b(k,G)-1}\qquad (X\to\infty),$$
where $a(G)=1/\min_{g\in G\setminus\{1\}}\operatorname{ind}(g)$ with $\operatorname{ind}(g)=n-\#\{\text{orbits of }\langle g\rangle\text{ on }\{1,\dots,n\}\}$.

(B) Batyrev–Manin conjecture (stacky form). Let $\mathcal{X}=[V/G]$ be a smooth Deligne–Mumford quotient stack over $k$ with $V$ a faithful $G$-representation, equipped with an anticanonical-type height $H\colon \mathcal{X}(k)\to\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ coming from the "raised line bundle" associated to the canonical sheaf. Let $U\subset\mathcal{X}$ be a suitable open substack. The Batyrev–Manin–Peyre conjecture predicts
$$\#\{x\in U(k): H(x)\le X\}\sim c_{\mathrm{Peyre}}(\mathcal{X})\,X^{\alpha(\mathcal{X})}(\log X)^{\beta(\mathcal{X})-1}\qquad (X\to\infty),$$
for explicit exponents $\alpha(\mathcal{X}),\beta(\mathcal{X})$ defined in terms of the anticanonical class and Picard group of $\mathcal{X}$, together with an explicit Peyre-type leading constant.

Conjectural relation. The two predictions are expected to coincide when $\mathcal{X}=[\mathbb{A}^n_k/G]$ with the regular permutation representation, in the sense that $k$-points of $[\mathbb{A}^n_k/G]$ counted by the canonical height correspond to $G$-extensions $K/k$ counted by absolute discriminant, and the exponents and constants on the two sides match.

Problem. Identify a nontrivial special case (a specific group $G$ and base $k$, or a specific family of stacks $\mathcal{X}$) for which one of conjectures (A) and (B) is already established, and derive from that case a previously unknown special case of the other conjecture. Equivalently: produce a rigorous implication "(A) for $(k,G)$" $\Rightarrow$ "(B) for $[\mathbb{A}^n_k/G]$", or vice versa, and verify it on at least one example beyond what is known directly.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of bridging Malle's conjecture and the (stacky) Batyrev–Manin–Peyre conjecture via the wild McKay correspondence is the subject of ongoing research. Follow-up work (e.g., Darda–Yasuda, "The Batyrev–Manin conjecture for DM stacks," 2022, and Part II, 2025) develops the stacky framework but does not establish the requested implication in general; no source claims to have proved a special case of one conjecture by using a known case of the other along these lines. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in the wild McKay correspondence and related fields
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 13.2. Prove one of the above two conjectures for some special case from the known case of the other conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: The Batyrev-Manin conjecture for DM stacks
status_evidence.snippet: We formulate a version of the Batyrev–Manin conjecture for Deligne–Mumford stacks that specializes to Malle's conjecture on the one hand and to the classical Batyrev–Manin conjecture on the other.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work unifies the two conjectures into a single framework but does not derive special cases of one from the other.

status_evidence.title: The Batyrev-Manin conjecture for DM stacks II
status_evidence.snippet: Continuation of the stacky Batyrev–Manin program; conjectural framework, partial results.
status_evidence.claim: The unification program remains at the level of conjectures and partial cases.
